chunks: And Ḥarīz narrated from Zurārah that al-Ḥakam asked Abū Jaʿfar عليه السلام
about a man to whom, in the Haram, a pigeon with clipped wings had been gifted. He عليه السلام said: “Pluck its feathers, feed it well, and when its feathers have grown back evenly, let it go.”

key_terms.الْحَرَمِ: the sacred sanctuary where special legal restrictions apply
key_terms.انْتِفْهَا: pluck it, i.e. remove the altered feathers
key_terms.سَبِيلَهَا: its way, meaning to let it go free
key_terms.عَلَفَهَا: its feed, meaning nourishment and care
key_terms.مَقْصُوصَةٌ: clipped, referring to its wings or feathers having been cut

ai.seo_question: What should be done with a pigeon with clipped wings that is gifted in the Haram?
ai.summary: This hadith gives a legal ruling concerning a pigeon with clipped wings in the Haram. The Imam عليه السلام instructs that it should be cared for until its feathers are restored, then released, reflecting both the sanctity of the Haram and proper treatment of the animal.

en.bab-ul-qaim-publications: Hadith.2359 - Hariz narrated from Zurara that Al-Hakam asked Abu Ja‘far (as) about a man who was gifted a pigeon with clipped wings in the Haram.
Imam (as) said: "Pluck its feathers, feed it well, and when its feathers have grown back, release it."
